_info: Hand-written starter list of common medical terms. Extend freely: add entries with 'term', optional 'aliases' and 'plain'. The explanations are general and do not replace a doctor's judgement.

entries.plain: a heart attack: part of the heart muscle is damaged because its blood supply was blocked
high blood pressure
low blood pressure
too much sugar (glucose) in the blood
too little sugar (glucose) in the blood
a long-term condition where the body cannot keep blood sugar at a healthy level
a form of diabetes where the body does not use insulin well, so blood sugar stays high
kidney damage or kidney disease
damage to the nerves, often causing pain, tingling or numbness
a stroke: blood flow to part of the brain is cut off or a blood vessel in the brain bursts
a blood clot forming inside a blood vessel
a blood clot in a deep vein, usually in the leg
a blood clot that blocks a blood vessel in the lungs
swelling caused by fluid building up in the body
shortness of breath or difficulty breathing
a faster than normal heartbeat
a slower than normal heartbeat
an irregular heartbeat
an irregular and often fast heartbeat that starts in the upper chambers of the heart
chest pain caused by the heart not getting enough blood
not enough blood supply to a part of the body
a lower than normal amount of red blood cells or hemoglobin, which can cause tiredness
related to the liver
related to the kidneys
related to the lungs
related to the heart
related to the heart and blood vessels
related to the stomach and intestines
a painkiller
a medicine that kills or stops the growth of bacteria
a blood thinner: a medicine that helps prevent blood clots
a medicine used to lower high blood pressure
a medicine that makes the body get rid of extra water and salt through urine
a medicine that reduces inflammation and calms the immune system
a dummy treatment with no active medicine, used for comparison in studies
a study where people are randomly put into groups to compare treatments fairly
not cancer and not likely to spread or become dangerous
cancerous and able to grow and spread
cancer that has spread from where it started to another part of the body
a type of cancer that starts in the skin or the lining of organs
an area of damaged or abnormal tissue
taking a small sample of tissue to look at under a microscope
the likely course and outcome of a disease
the cause of a disease
illness or health problems caused by a disease or treatment
death rate
how many new cases of a condition appear in a certain time
how many people have a condition at a given time
having no symptoms
sudden and short-lasting, often severe
lasting a long time or coming back again and again
having no known cause
should not be used because it could cause harm
an unwanted side effect
how well a treatment works
another health condition that a person has at the same time
a life-threatening reaction of the body to an infection
an infection of the lungs
a long-term lung disease that makes it hard to breathe
a scan that uses X-rays to make detailed pictures of the inside of the body
a scan that uses magnets and radio waves to make detailed pictures of the inside of the body
a test that records the electrical activity of the heart
a number that compares weight with height
a blood test showing the average blood sugar level over the past 2-3 months
the top blood pressure number: the pressure when the heart pumps
the bottom blood pressure number: the pressure when the heart rests between beats
a result that is unlikely to be due to chance alone
